profile.name: Leah Demo
profile.audience: Hobby bookbinders and small community libraries
profile.ideal_customer: A beginner who wants to repair their own ordinary notebooks
business_goals: Help suitable beginners understand how the workshops work
career_history: Fictional bookbinder for software acceptance testing
strong_opinions: The halfway-through repair can teach more than the finished cover
profile.desired_tone: Warm, observant and plain, with occasional dry humor. Sentence case.
writing_samples: I put a strip of scrap paper under the hinge before I reach for glue. If the paper catches, something is rubbing. More glue will not make the book open politely.
Today’s repair looked worse halfway through. That is usually when I take a photo. The tidy finished cover hides the useful bit: where the old cloth split and how the new hinge sits.
A square of scrap cloth is a perfectly respectable place to make a mistake. Try the fold there first. The notebook can wait five minutes.
reference_creators: An unrelated fictional marketing writer whose loud style is not mine
profile.cta_offer: Mention workshops only when explicitly requested
restrictions: Fictional QA creator and source material
Do not claim a visitor’s business results
Do not give conservation advice for valuable or historic books

cases.voice:
# Voice

Fictional Leah Demo. Sentence case; warm, observant, plain. Start with the physical object or action. Humor is optional and should grow from the object. No appended joke, sales pitch, abstract life lesson or default CTA.
cases.source:
Leah: My blank record for an ordinary practice notebook has these headings: notebook label, date, what moves, what catches, what I tried, next observation.
Leah: I record an action only after I have tried it. If I have not tried anything, that field stays blank.
Leah: I have not measured time saved or repair success. These headings record a decision; they do not prescribe a treatment. Valuable or historic books are outside this beginner workshop.
cases.topic: Set up a practice notebook record
cases.brief: Write a practical LinkedIn post that lets a beginner set up this record today. Use the source and creator voice.

rubric.question: Does the post deliver a copyable practice record with its material scope intact, without inventing outcomes or loading the public prose with internal evidence-audit notes that do not help use the record?

cases.source:
Leah: I want to test whether a blank note template gets more saves than a finished-cover description on X.
Leah: I have drafted the two versions but have not published them or collected any results.
Leah: My next step is to decide an observation window and record saves and impressions for both versions.
cases.topic: A planned comparison of two X posts
cases.brief: Write an update on this content experiment. Say what is known and what comes next.

rubric.question: Does the draft preserve that this is an unrun test with no results, rather than removing the qualification or making a save-rate improvement sound established?
